operation.description: Raise the cumulative supply ceiling 50,000 -> 80,000 USDC and replace operator A with operator B, with 30,000 already consumed.

parity._note: Held performs three REAL 10,000 USDC supplies through its own controller so it starts from the SAME 30,000 consumed / 20,000 remaining the native baseline starts from. Asserted, not assumed.

isolation: evm_snapshot before each branch, evm_revert after, so the clean and interrupted cases cannot contaminate each other.
accounting: ONE method. Every ceremony is a real Safe execTransaction signed by two of three owners; the change is a real MultiSendCallOnly delegatecall. Nothing is counted as batched that was not batched.

findings.detail: native 1/2/1 against Held 2/4/2. Held cannot batch fence with activate: the controller refuses to activate while active, and the fence must be CONFIRMED before a candidate is pinned. A product constraint, not an accounting artifact.
native 2/4/2 against Held 2/4/2. The competent native procedure reaches the correct result on the first attempt and costs the same.

findings.dimension: stores consulted to resolve an in-flight operation
findings.detail: Held answers 'did THAT operation execute?' from 1 store: consumed[operationId] at a stated block, bound to the native decision by the journal. Native derives the BUDGET correctly in aggregate from the allowance but does not identify which operation ran.
findings.caveat: Native reaches the correct remaining capacity without this.

findings.dimension: behaviour when the outcome is unknown
findings.result: HELD REFUSES; NATIVE HAS NOTHING TO REFUSE WITH
findings.detail: the interrupted branch raised 1 refusal(s) naming the unresolved operation and would not advance. Native has no per-operation record, so there is no state in which it can decline.
findings.caveat: A property of the SYSTEM, not the operator. A careful native operator following the V4 order reaches the same outcome.

findings.result: HELD ENFORCES SOMETHING NATIVE DOES NOT
findings.detail: The controller refuses an activation whose ceiling the Zodiac allowance would not honour (AllowanceDesynchronised), which is why the change batch must carry setAllowance and activate together.
findings.caveat: Makes one specific operator error impossible rather than unlikely.

findings.detail: A controller deployed and installed, sole membership of two Zodiac roles, five budgets configured, and a durable journal.

conclusion.headline: Held does not reduce owner work. It costs more on the clean change and ties competent native tooling on the interrupted one.
held_adds: a refusal the system enforces while an outcome is unknown
held_costs: more owner work on a clean change
controller, two role memberships, five budgets, a journal
a further component to trust and maintain
conclusion.what_is_NOT_claimed: That Held is cheaper or faster, or that native tooling cannot do this. The measurements say otherwise.

interruption_semantics._warning: The two interrupted branches do NOT share an interruption, and their final remaining figures must not be compared as if they did.
interruption_semantics.native_I2: an in-flight supply that DID land (5,000 more consumed), so the competent procedure derives 35,000 used and 45,000 remaining.
interruption_semantics.held: a submission whose transport never returned and which did NOT reach the chain, so consumption stays at 30,000 and 50,000 remains.
interruption_semantics.what_this_does_and_does_not_show: Both branches reach the CORRECT remaining capacity for the interruption they actually suffered. Neither preserved more than the other; they faced different events.

limits: Local Base-mainnet fork only. No public transaction, deployment or spending.
Operator-work counts are counts of discrete contract-level actions, as the native baseline states of its own numbers. Not a human-factors study.
The native half was measured before Held existed; the halves were not run simultaneously. The operation, counters and starting state are the same.
Almanak reconfiguration and the authenticated KeeperHub boundary are exercised on neither side. L10 is open.
